name: War-Risk Insurance and Freight Cost Pressure
situation: Red Sea and global shipping disruption

definition.question: How elevated are war-risk premiums and freight costs for shipping through threatened chokepoints?
definition.low_end: War-risk premiums and freight rates are at normal baseline levels with readily available insurance and no chokepoint surcharges.
definition.high_end: War-risk premiums and freight rates spike to prohibitive levels, insurance becomes unavailable or highly conditional, and most owners refuse chokepoint transits on cost/risk grounds.

readings.rationale: London market war-risk premiums for Hormuz transits rose to ~2-6% of vessel value, with earlier periods up to 10%, with fewer inquiries as owners grew reluctant and traffic drops driven by operator caution not just physical blockade; Houthi embargo is assessed as likely to raise shipping costs and disrupt Saudi oil exports via Red Sea. Higher if Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb premiums exceed 6-10% broadly…

No_change: past 65 already captured Hormuz war-risk 2-6% (up to 10%) and owner reluctance; new evidence confirms prolonged Hormuz disruption but provides no new Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb premium quotes or withdrawal to justify move above 65.
